messages:
maria.g: Quick follow-up from the MHA layout RFC review — we need to pick a default tiling pattern for the runtime. I sketched three options and their runtime implications.
sam.k: Thanks Maria. Can you list the options briefly? I skimmed the doc but want the perf impact summary.
maria.g: Sure. Option A: token-major contiguous QKV (NHWC-like): QKV interleaved per token, contiguous in memory. Pros: simple continuous loads for kernels, good prefetching. Cons: poor head-wise vectorization and awkward SIMD when heads are processed separately.
linus: Option B: head-major contiguous (NCHW-like) — all heads for a token stored in separate planes. Pros: head-parallel kernels map nicely, easier per-head quantization adjustments. Cons: strided loads when doing token-major batched GEMMs, more cache-line thrash for long sequences.
maya: Option C: blocked/tiling hybrid — pack small head blocks (e.g., 4 heads together) contiguous, then stride between blocks. Think of it as compromise between A/B.
maria.g: Bandwidth/latency tradeoffs we saw in microbenchmarks:

```
setup: A100, seq=1024, bsz=8, heads=32, d_head=64
A (token-major): 1.0x baseline latency, good single-request latency
B (head-major): 0.85x latency in multi-head-parallel kernels, 1.25x for token-major fallback
C (blocked 4): 0.92x steady, best cache reuse across short/long sequences
```

These are illustrative — numbers vary with kernel implementation.
sam.k: So runtime kernel selector needs to pick per-request layout or provide cheap in-place reorder? We cannot pay large reorder cost for every request.
linus: Reorder cost depends on where it's done. Two choices:
 1) JIT reorder at request ingress (pay once): convert incoming layout -> engine-preferred contiguous blocks
 2) Lazy on-demand in kernel via strided loads (no reorder but higher per-token cost)
maya: For Dedicated customers with steady throughput, a one-time ingress reorder amortizes well. For hosted short-tail traffic, strided kernel is better to avoid memory copies.
maria.g: That's what I was thinking. Also impacts KV cache shape and snapshotting: head-major cache allows cheaper per-head eviction but complicates prefix caching when we tile heads differently.
linus: Another subtlety: quantized kernels (INT8/4) prefer contiguous packed tails for packing kernels. If we default to token-major, we force packing step inside infer kernel.
sam.k: Actionables?
maria.g: Proposal:
 - Default internal layout: blocked (C) with block_size=4 for general builds.
 - Kernel selector policy: if request seq_len>512 and throughput>threshold, prefer head-major kernels (B) and trigger ingress reorder async.
 - For hosted low-latency requests (<100ms target), avoid reorder and use token-major fast-path.
 - Add a lightweight runtime metric 'reorder_overhead_ms' and flag per-model so we can iterate.
maya: +1. Also add a flag for customers to pin layout if they manage custom kernels.
linus: I'll mock kernel selector heuristics and add microbench harness for head sizes 16/32/64.
bench-bot: perf job queued: perf/mha-tiling/1729460000
sam.k: Sounds good. Can you put the selector decision table into the RFC follow-up doc and include the perf harness commands? I want to review before we lock defaults.
maria.g: Will do. I'll drop the follow-up doc and a short checklist for Dedicated/Hosted differences. Thanks all.
